TASK A (ROLE/PERSONA routing): build seeded domain-structured worlds with roles {scientist, engineer, business analyst, executive/C-suite, financial analyst/planner, commodities analyst, economist, linguist, psychologist, historian/humanities} where each task has a domain/sub-skill and graded quality depends on (i) hidden per-agent competence per domain and (ii) whether the agent is invoked in a role-conditioned context that matches the task (role-conditioning adds a modest, parameterised quality bonus ONLY on matching tasks and a small penalty on mismatches/ceremonial prompts — state this assumption explicitly, test sensitivity incl. a world where role-conditioning has ZERO effect, and one where it is harmful). Compare: generic path, oracle role, learned role routing (route to role by task text/anchors/keywords), role x agent joint routing, role routing with a role-confidence gate, vs best fair baseline set. Honest expectation: pure persona-routing is marginal; measure it. B (DOMAIN-CORPUS RETRIEVAL): build local corpora per domain from REAL text available on disk where possible (e.g. vendored crate docs on STEM-ish/crypto/numerics; the repo's research docs; plus any other real text you can find legitimately on disk without network — list what you used; for finance/economics/politics/psychology/linguistics domains with no real text on disk, use clearly-labelled seeded synthetic domain corpora) and test whether domain-partitioned/domain-prioritised retrieval (domain router -> domain index vs pooled index; hybrid z+spell) improves downstream research-task quality held-out vs pooled retrieval and vs no retrieval, including cross-domain confusable queries and a no-domain-structure control. Report retrieval metrics + end-to-end quality. Protocol: tune 1-8, held 31-60, confirm 61-90, Holm, >=2 independent generators; controls harmless (TOST +-0.01).

handback.t:
R9-D (H20) is finished, and both headline effects are conditional on outcome models I wrote. Persona routing is marginal, as expected, and domain-prioritised retrieval improves context purity, not recall. No src edits, no commits, no downloads. I used Python rather than Rust bins (`py/h20_*`). The hybrid z(.7)+BM25+spell pipeline is a replica of `src/hybrid.rs` whose agreement with the Rust code I did not verify. Baselines are Python eps-greedy, Gaussian-Thompson and keyword-table variants; hebbian-robust, warm and guarded-safe were not run.

Everything is labelled synthetic-until-validated. Reruns are byte-identical (verified for retrieval confirm and persona confirm). Protocol: tune seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60, confirm 61-90 with config frozen, Holm, TOST ±0.01 on controls.

**A. Persona routing** (`py/h20_persona.py`)
- **Assumption:** quality = competence + role term + noise. The role term is bonus b×responsiveness minus ceremonial cost c when the role matches the task domain, and −p − c when it does not.
- **Worlds:** effect worlds mod (b=.05), zero, harm (b=−.03), strong (b=.12) and hetero (per-agent responsiveness). Generators G1 (specialist agents, templated text) and G2 (latent-factor agents, noisy text), plus a control with identical agents. Ten roles from your list.
- **Pure persona effect is arithmetic:** gain ≈ detection accuracy × b − (1−acc) × p.
  - Oracle role gives +.045 (G1-mod) and +.050 (control, exactly b).
  - Keyword-anchor role gives +.025/+.031 (held/confirm) in G1-mod at accuracy .83, up to +.076 at b=.12.
  - It is exactly 0 at b=0 and −.034..−.058 when the role is harmful.
  - Agent routing headroom (~.2: best baseline ≈.64 vs a best-agent ceiling of .87) is 4–10× the whole persona effect.
- **Learned role routing loses** whenever the role has a real effect (−.009..−.028, Holm-significant).
- **Joint role×agent is positive but slow** (+.008..+.039), and it is not harmful in the harm worlds (−.004..−.008, not significant).
- **Online randomised A/B confidence gate is the only role policy safe everywhere.**
  - It is TOST-equivalent to the baseline in the zero worlds and in the harm worlds on confirm (G1-harm was −.004 Holm-significant on held, −.001 on confirm).
  - It recovers only ~25% of a real effect inside 1000 tasks (+.007 vs +.031 for ungated anchor in G1-mod), firing on 11–23% of calls.
  - Per-agent gating adds nothing, even in the hetero world.
- **Static margin gate:** tuned to essentially never fire (tau 4), because the tuning objective was mean plus worst-case world.
- **Holm-significant contrasts:** 32/70 held, 28/70 confirm.

**B. Domain-corpus retrieval** (`py/h20_corpus.py`, `h20_syn.py`, `h20_embed.py`, `h20_retrieval.py`)
- **Real text used:**
  - `pydoc9`: docstring prose of installed Python packages, parsed with `ast` and never executed. Seven domains: numerics_stats, ml_data, language_text, graph_knowledge, web_network, db_cloud, and this repo's research docs.
  - `crates8`: README and `//!` docs of the 1200 vendored crates, labelled by each crate's own `Cargo.toml` categories. Seven domains.
  - Crypto and time/decimal domains had too little usable text and were dropped.
- **Synthetic:** `syn10`, labelled, for the ten role domains with no real text on disk (finance, economics, commodities, psychology, linguistics, history and so on).
- **Embeddings:** on-disk MiniLM via the cognee-venv onnxruntime.
- **Controls:** domain labels randomly permuted (no domain structure).
- **Quality model (assumption):** q = base + 0.30×hit@5 − 0.10×off-domain share of the five contexts + noise.
- **Frozen arm (tune pick):** pooled hybrid plus a domain prior from the kNN vote of the pooled top-10 (lambda 16, a plateau from 8 to 16). All domain arms are switched off by a pre-declared label-structure self-check.
- **End-to-end gain vs the best fair pooled baseline (hybrid+spell):**

| World | Held | Confirm |
|---|---|---|
| pydoc9 | +.0167 | +.0098 |
| crates8 | +.0161 | +.0206 |
| syn10 | +.0001 | −.0009 (TOST-equivalent) |

  - The two real-text gains are Holm-significant on confirm.
- **The gain comes entirely from the assumed off-domain harm term.**
  - hit@5 is −.011..+.007 and MRR is about 0.
  - Off-domain context drops 27%→13% (pydoc9) and 41%→21% (crates8).
  - With harm set to 0 the gain is +.002/−.003/0 (`results/h20_retrieval_sens_held.json`).
  - On the confusable-query tertile the prior costs hit@5 (−.016/−.046 on confirm).
- **Oracle headroom:** true-domain labels would give +.04..+.08 end-to-end. The router realises about 25–40% of that, and none of the recall.
- **Synthetic world:** `syn10` has no headroom for domain partitioning, the templated-corpus failure mode again.
- **Controls:** with no domain structure the self-check disables the domain arms and they are identical to pooled. That is a tie by construction of the guard, not evidence the router is harmless. Without the check the same arm loses hit@5 by .07–.11 and quality by .02–.04.
- **Hybrid over dense+spell replicated:** confirm hit@5 .63/.64/.37 vs .54/.59/.26.
- **Spell on this 50%-typo mix:** hit@5 +.007..+.023 on the real worlds.

**Disclosed post-hoc changes**
- I saw the first-pass held-out results before changing the retrieval controls' harm model (now charged against the true domain) and adding logistic-regression routers. Tune picked the same arm, and confirm was never seen before the freeze.
- I also saw the first persona held-out results before separating the role-exploration RNG stream from the agent-selection stream and widening the gate grid.
- First-pass logs are kept (`results/h20_v1_logs/`, `h20_retrieval_held_v1.*`).
- Tuned values at grid edges are listed in the board entry.
